title: Event-sieve + continuation-token middleware for Python SDK streaming chat
creator: Nina Alvarez
description:
Problem: Customers integrating long-lived streaming chat sessions report difficulty reconciling partial state after transient network failures, duplicate fragments, and client-side filters (eg. profanity or signal-based trimming). Existing SDK patterns focus on general checkpointing or replay but lack a lightweight, composable middleware that simultaneously: 1) filters irrelevant events early in the pipeline (reducing client work and telemetry noise), 2) emits compact continuation tokens that capture just the minimal resume point and necessary sideband metadata, and 3) provides deterministic idempotent application semantics so resumed sessions do not double-apply fragments.

Goal: Implement an "event-sieve + continuation-token" middleware for the Python SDK that offers an ergonomic hook for user filters, produces small continuation tokens for network-resume, and integrates with our telemetry and retry policies. The middleware should be easy to opt into, compatible with sync/async streaming surfaces, and include examples showing common patterns (signal filtering, incremental metrics, and safe partial-output commits).
acceptance_criteria: Supports both sync generator and async iterator streaming APIs without API surface divergence
Continuation token format is compact (<= 1KB typical), forward-compatible, and documented
Resuming a stream with a continuation token results in deterministic output: no duplicate final messages or double-applied side effects for configured idempotent sinks
Configurable filtering DSL exposed to customers (predicate function or declarative match rules)
End-to-end integration test coverage: network disconnect + resume, event filter change and stable resume behavior, telemetry counters emitted
Performance overhead measured: median added latency per-event < 250us on p3-like hardware for default sieve
Docs + example notebook and two sample recipes merged to docs site and python sdk examples repo
Design reviewed and security_review_required flagged if continuation token contains PII
technical_notes: Continuation token model: opaque base64 JSON with fields: last_event_id, ordered_watermark, small sideband checksums for prefix hash, optional filter-version tag
Event sieve: chainable pipeline stage executed before user callbacks; accepts predicate(fn(event) -> bool) and transformer(fn(event) -> event) hooks
Idempotency: recommend sink contract where each sink implements apply(event_id, event_payload) -> commit_token; middleware will track commit_token in continuation token to avoid reapply
Sync/async compatibility: implement core logic in sync functions, provide async wrappers using to_thread or async generators to avoid duplicating complex logic
Backpressure: sieve must be non-blocking by default; heavy predicates should run on executor and exposed to users in examples
Telemetry: emit counters 'sieve.dropped', 'sieve.passed', 'continuation.issued', 'continuation.resumed', plus histograms for token_size_bytes and resume_latency_ms
Security: continuation token will be signed with HMAC using SDK key store; if PII allowed by user config, require explicit opt-in and mark token as sensitive in logs
Backward compatibility: token parser will accept previous format versions; include migration tests
Fallback: when continuation not accepted by server, SDK should attempt full-replay path with a bounded retry and consult user-provided conflict handler

comments: 2026-03-02 Nina Alvarez: Initial write-up and prototype with two predicate styles (callable and simple DSL). Prototype uses naive JSON continuation token with last_event_index and prefix_hash.
2026-03-04 Samir Patel: Benchmarked prototype; baseline per-event overhead ~180us when predicate is simple attribute check. Noted that heavy regex predicates add 1-2ms unless executed in threadpool.

2026-03-06 Security review: flagged continuation token signing and opt-in for PII. Decided to sign tokens with SDK HMAC and mark opt-in path. Samir to add KMS integration ticket if customer requests server-verified tokens.

2026-03-08 Design review notes: prefer minimal state in token (last_event_id + sink_commit_hint) over full prefix. Add 'filter_version' tag so changing customer predicate invalidates resume by default.

2026-03-09 QA: Wrote resume integration test harness simulating interleaved partial-fragment and network drop. Found edge case where server replay injects finalization event; added conflict handler hook to allow client to decide merge or replace.
2026-03-10 Samir Patel: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/1289 (WIP). Planning docs and cookbook next.
